digest.component_or_area: enrichment queue and ticket digest event storage
propositions: Physical deletion of committed UUID events from the enrichment queue breaks cross-clone merges via git rename detection (CONFLICT rename/rename) when two clones independently delete the same file and add distinct new files with different UUIDs

Deleting committed files reclaims zero repository space because the blobs remain in git history; prune reduces only working-tree checkout size (~2% of 251 MB) while adding deletion commits and breaking reconvergence

The queue reduce reader (_events_of) opens all matching files per type per ticket (4,977 opens across 11,181 listdir calls on a 3,727-ticket store); a newest-first suffix-lazy read bounds this to 1,658 opens by reading only the newest event file per type

A merge-safe retention scheme must rename to a deterministic source-derived path with identical content (as compact.py does with RETIRED_SUFFIX), never to a UUID-derived path, to ensure both clones compute the same target deterministically

The designed read-bound approach is merge-safe by construction because it is read-only—removing, renaming, and writing nothing—therefore preserving invariant I1 and leaving cross-clone reconvergence unchanged

The filename prefix ({timestamp}-{uuid}-{TYPE}.json) equals the event body's monotonic timestamp, making lexicographic filename order equivalent to timestamp order, enabling O(1) newest-event reads without history scan
